message:
I see - `q_read` reads `n` bytes into `buf` (which is `ifp->rx.buf` of size 1540). The `q_write` function checks `len + sizeof(size_t) <= left` where `left` is the available space in the queue. The queue is 16KB, so packets up to ~16KB could be queued. But `q_read` copies `n` bytes into `ifp->rx.buf` which is only 1540 bytes. So if a packet larger than 1540 bytes is queued, `q_read` would overflow `ifp->rx.buf`.

But wait, the `on_rx` function is called by the driver with the actual received packet. Let me check how the driver receives packets. Let me look at the test harness or how this is being tested:

<｜｜DSML｜｜=execute_bash>
<parameter=command>find /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul -name "*.c" -o -name "*.cc" -o -name "*.h" | xargs grep -ln "mip_init\|mip_rx\|on_rx" 2>/dev/null | head -20</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
